summary: A switch for an on/off setting, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the switch and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps external <label for> from reaching the inner input.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the switch.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

value.note: Submitted with the form while on.

checked.note: Current state (on). Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Native required: must be on. Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled; dimmed; not submitted. Also set by a disabled <fieldset> ancestor without changing the attribute.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: switch in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Switch wrapper; positions the thumb over the native input.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">, drawn as the track; receives focus, Space and validation.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Decorative, aria-hidden. Moves from the start to the end edge when on.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track filled with the primary color and the thumb at the end edge; position, not color alone, shows the state (WCAG 1.4.1).

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or a disabled <fieldset> ancestor

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: FormAssociated mixin (ElementInternals): setFormValue(value) only while on, validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing), formResetCallback restores the default checked state, disabled (own or fieldset) is not submitted, formStateRestore restores checked. validationAnchor is the inner input, so reportValidity() focuses it.

accessibility.targetSize: Track is 32x20px (default) and 24x16px (sm); the label next to it is part of the clickable row and the gap satisfies the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception for the sm track.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty (NativeControl).

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009); it does not toggle

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox input, which exposes aria-checked from its checked state
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A setting with two states that takes effect as soon as it is flipped
The setting needs its effect explained
A choice must be on before the form can be submitted
useCases.use: required with a label that states what is turned on

useCases.when: A compact row such as a settings list

antiPatterns.pattern: A yes/no answer submitted later with the form, such as accepting terms
antiPatterns.why: A switch implies an immediate effect; the choice is recorded, not applied
A switch has two states only

antiPatterns.pattern: A pressed-state button in a toolbar
antiPatterns.why: A switch is a form control with a name and a value; a toolbar button has no form value

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: the visual reference for the look and sizes, the APG switch pattern for keyboard and ARIA, the Checkbox contract for the shared label, description, error and form behavior.

openQuestions.question: Native <input type=checkbox role=switch> or a custom button with role=switch?
openQuestions.answer: Native checkbox input with role=switch (recommended): it gives Space, focus, required validity and the form owner for free, and the hooks of NativeControl already wrap it.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch?
openQuestions.answer: No (recommended). The APG makes Enter optional; Space toggles and Enter submits the form like a native checkbox (SB-0009), matching Checkbox.

openQuestions.question: Is label required, and may it be hidden?
openQuestions.answer: Required, like Checkbox and Input. hide-label hides it visually and keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No (recommended). The attribute is the default that form reset restores, as in Checkbox; checked is a property and the attribute is read at start.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes?
openQuestions.answer: default and sm, as in the visual reference, registered as aliases of the canonical size values medium and small. Track dimensions come from the existing size.switch.* semantic tokens.

openQuestions.question: How does the error behave and where does the label sit?
openQuestions.answer: The error sets a customError validity so the form blocks submission, is shown in a persistent polite live region and marks aria-invalid, as in Checkbox. The label sits after the switch, with description and error under it.

openQuestions.question: Should the switch show on/off text or icons?
openQuestions.answer: No (recommended). Thumb position and the switch role convey the state; text belongs in the label. Not needed for WCAG 1.4.1 because position is not color alone.
